headline: Strong high pressure keeps both regions dry through Thursday as sunshine drives a steady warm-up; patchy Kentucky valley fog and localized frost remain the only near-term concerns
disclaimer: Independent amateur analysis. This is not an official forecast or warning. Follow the National Weather Service and local authorities during hazardous weather.

refresh.workflow: Update and commit forecast.json once. GitHub Actions automatically locks the prior issue in forecast-history.json. Then verify the GitHub Pages URL; every Google Sites embed reads the same file and refreshes automatically.

kentucky.name: Central Kentucky
kentucky.subtitle: Danville primary · Lexington comparison
kentucky.summary: A strong surface anticyclone and a very dry middle atmosphere suppress clouds and precipitation through Thursday. The upper-ridge axis crosses the Ohio Valley Wednesday evening, allowing shallow southerly flow and warm-air advection to raise afternoon temperatures several degrees each day. Clear sky and weak wind still permit strong nighttime cooling in Danville-area valleys, with patchy fog and localized frost or a freeze most likely tonight.
kentucky.currentConditions: At 8:15 AM EST, KDVK reported 32°F with a 30°F dew point, calm wind, clear sky and visibility above 10 miles. At 8:00 AM, KLEX reported 32°F with a 30°F dew point, calm wind, clear sky and 6-mile visibility in mist. No official NWS point alert was active for Danville at the final issuance check.

days.label: Tuesday / Tuesday night
days.hazard: OFFICIAL NWS ALERT STATUS: no active point alert covers Danville at issuance. Independent concerns are patchy river-valley fog late tonight and localized frost or a freeze in colder valleys. Widespread dense fog is not forecast.
days.forecast: Sunshine and strong subsidence bring a dry day with a most-likely Danville high near 58°F. Light and variable wind around 0–5 mph becomes calm tonight. The most-likely Wednesday-morning low is near 33°F, with rural valleys falling into the upper 20s. Patchy valley fog is most plausible from about 1–8 AM EST, especially near rivers and sheltered low spots.

days.label: Wednesday / Wednesday night
days.hazard: No official NWS point alert covers Wednesday at issuance. Independent concerns are isolated late-night valley fog and a localized rural frost or freeze; rain, thunder and hazardous wind are not forecast.
days.forecast: Any shallow valley fog clears quickly, followed by full sunshine and a most-likely high near 63°F. Southeast wind remains light around 1–6 mph. Mostly clear conditions continue Wednesday night with a most-likely low near 36–37°F; a few colder Danville-area valleys may briefly reach freezing.

days.label: Thursday / early Friday
days.hazard: No official NWS point alert covers Thursday at issuance. No widespread hazardous weather is expected. Patchy river-valley fog may redevelop toward Friday morning, and the coldest sheltered pocket could see frost.
days.forecast: The upper ridge and shallow southerly flow support another sunny, dry and milder day. The most-likely Danville high is near 65–66°F with wind around 0–6 mph. A few high clouds may arrive Thursday night. The most-likely early-Friday low is near 40–41°F, with colder valleys in the upper 30s. Patchy fog is possible mainly from about 1–8 AM EST Friday.

kentucky.bottomLine: Central Kentucky stays dry and increasingly mild through Thursday. Most-likely Danville high/low pairs are 58/33°F, 63/36–37°F and 65–66/40–41°F. Patchy valley fog and localized frost or a freeze tonight are the main concerns; the cold risk diminishes as the air mass moderates.
kentucky.confidence: High for dry weather and the warming trend; high for daytime temperatures; moderate for exact valley lows and the localized coverage of fog

upstate.name: Upstate South Carolina
upstate.subtitle: Clemson primary · Central/Pickens County comparison
upstate.summary: Strong high pressure centered over the central Appalachians and Mid-Atlantic keeps the Clemson–Central corridor dry through Thursday. Rising upper-level heights support a steady warm-up, while persistent northeast flow limits humidity and keeps wind below hazard levels. Moisture begins to increase Thursday, but subsidence remains dominant and only additional clouds—not meaningful rain—are expected within this forecast.
upstate.currentConditions: At 8:00 AM EST, KCEU reported 38°F with a 36°F dew point, calm wind, clear sky and 9-mile visibility, along with an automated trace light-rain code. Radar, satellite, KLQK and KGSP did not support regional precipitation, so the trace was treated as an isolated sensor or frost-related report. At 8:15 AM, KLQK reported 33°F with a 32°F dew point, light northeast wind, clear sky and visibility above 10 miles. No official NWS point alert was active for Clemson or Central. Tempest data was not used.

days.label: Tuesday / Tuesday night
days.hazard: OFFICIAL NWS ALERT STATUS: no active point alert covers Clemson or Central at issuance. Independent concern is patchy frost or an isolated freeze late tonight around KLQK and the coldest sheltered Pickens County valleys. No regional rain event is forecast.
days.forecast: Sunny, dry weather continues beneath strong high pressure. The corridor's most-likely high is near 61°F with east-northeast wind around 3–8 mph and occasional gusts of 12–17 mph. Most-likely Wednesday-morning lows are near 38°F at KCEU and 34°F at KLQK, with the coldest hollows near freezing.

days.label: Wednesday / Wednesday night
days.hazard: No official NWS point alert covers Wednesday at issuance. No widespread hazardous weather is expected. An isolated colder hollow could develop frost, but a corridor-wide freeze, rain and hazardous wind are not forecast.
days.forecast: Sunshine and rising upper-level heights continue the warm-up, with a most-likely corridor high near 64–65°F. Northeast wind runs around 4–9 mph with occasional gusts of 15–20 mph. Mostly clear conditions persist Wednesday night; most-likely lows are near 44°F at KCEU and 40°F at KLQK.

days.label: Thursday / early Friday
days.hazard: No official NWS point alert covers Thursday at issuance. No hazardous weather is expected. A minority of ensemble members produce a trace of rain, but official and deterministic guidance keep meaningful precipitation unlikely through early Friday.
days.forecast: Mostly sunny conditions and a most-likely high near 66°F are expected. Northeast wind around 5–10 mph may gust 15–20 mph. Moisture increases modestly and high clouds may thicken late, but subsidence should prevent meaningful rain. Most-likely early-Friday lows are near 50°F at KCEU and 46°F at KLQK.

upstate.bottomLine: The Clemson–Central corridor remains dry and warms steadily through Thursday. Most-likely high/low pairs are 61/38°F at Clemson and 61/34°F at Central tonight, 64–65/44 and 40°F Wednesday, and 66/50 and 46°F Thursday. Patchy frost is possible tonight in the coldest Central/Pickens valleys; otherwise impacts are minimal.
upstate.confidence: High for dry weather and the warming trend; high for daytime temperatures; moderate-high for the overnight station split and Thursday cloud coverage

sourceNotes: OFFICIAL ALERTS: no active NWS point alert was present for Danville, Clemson or Central at the final issuance check. Official alerts remain separate from outlooks and this independent analysis.
The 11:05Z Louisville discussion supports early valley fog, possible freezing fog in cold pockets, dominant high pressure, dry weather through Friday, abundant sunshine and warming temperatures.

Chris Bailey’s November 17 Kentucky Weather Center post, ‘All Eyes on Thanksgiving Week Changes,’ was accepted as authoritative published source material. Bailey calls the current period an amazing week and specifically supports Thursday highs in the 60s. His storm discussion begins beyond this 72-hour forecast; details absent from the post or unreadable in graphics were left unknown.

The 11:23Z Greenville-Spartanburg discussion supports dry weather through Friday, strong high pressure, warming temperatures, possible additional clouds Thursday and very low precipitation probabilities.
Official point guidance supports Danville near 58/34°F, 63/37°F and 66/41°F; Clemson near 62/36°F, 65/42°F and 66/48°F; and Central near 61/36°F, 64/42°F and 66/48°F.
COD radar at 13:30Z showed no precipitation near either corridor, while visible and infrared imagery at 13:31Z showed the inland Southeast largely clear.

KCEU encoded a trace light-rain report with zero measurable precipitation and clear sky. With no radar, satellite or neighboring-station support, it was treated as an isolated sensor or frost-related trace rather than a regional precipitation event.

Every currently available COD family was audited: HRRR, RAP, RRFS, GEM-RDPS, GEM-GDPS, ECMWF, GFS, AIFS, AIGFS, CFSv2, GEFS, REFS, AIFS-ENS and AIGEFS. NAM and NAM Nest are retired; retained November 3 files were stale and excluded.

Fresh deterministic, AI, regional and ensemble guidance supports dry weather through Thursday. The minority GEFS wet signal in the Upstate Thursday is retained as a 5–10% probability rather than treated as a material conflict.

The installed BUFKIT 19 data were refreshed and validated at 13:37–13:40Z. GFS 06Z, HRRR/RAP 11Z and locally converted RRFS 06Z profiles were used; all were dry and stable with no CAPE and light surface wind.
Fresh RRFS profiles extend through 18Z November 20. Partial HRRR and RAP horizons were not extrapolated beyond their available data.
The maintained KDVK −1.5°F low correction and current Kentucky empirical widths were applied to the nighttime ranges. Terrain spread remains larger than daytime model spread.
The maintained KCEU +1.5°F and KLQK −3°F low corrections preserve a warmer Clemson and colder Central/Pickens nighttime split inside the current 10°F regional ranges.
WPC’s relevant excessive-rain risk is confined to Florida, and no supported thunder, heavy-rain, flooding or hazardous-wind signal covers either forecast corridor.
The latest completed accuracy summary contains 149 verified checkpoints and all-category accuracy of 80.9% overall, including 84.3% for Central Kentucky and 77.3% for the Upstate.
Current station corrections, empirical lead-specific widths, verified model weighting, calibrated confidence, explicit fog windows and official-alert separation were applied.
Temperature cards use the current calibrated widths: Kentucky highs of 5/5/6°F and lows of 8°F; Upstate highs of 4/5/6°F and lows of 10°F. Prose supplies narrower station-specific most-likely values.
All local times use Eastern Standard Time. The third card includes Thursday night and early Friday because validThrough is exactly 72 elapsed hours after issuance.
Contains modified ECMWF Open Data, selected and processed for independent forecast research under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0).
Tempest data was not used for Upstate observations, verification, calibration or adjustment.
This is a candidate only. No repository, forecast history, website, widget or publishing workflow was modified during preparation.
